references.text: God commands Noah to bring two of every living creature into the ark to keep them alive during the flood, including birds, livestock, and creeping things.
God instructs Noah to take seven pairs of each clean animal and bird, and one pair of the unclean animals, highlighting the distinction between clean and unclean creatures.
After the flood, God commands Noah to release all the animals from the ark—birds, livestock, and creeping things—so that they may multiply on the earth.
In Leviticus, detailed laws are given regarding which animals are clean and unclean, expanding on distinctions already hinted at in Noah's time.
In Deuteronomy, the laws concerning clean and unclean animals are repeated, showing that this distinction has deep roots dating back to before the flood.

In Acts, Peter sees a vision of a sheet coming down from heaven containing all kinds of four-footed animals and creeping things, where God declares that the distinction between clean and unclean has been abolished.
Genesis 7:8 shows the historical division that Leviticus 20:25 later forbids Israel from breaking.
The identical categorization of creatures in the ark presupposes the later legislation found in Leviticus.
The list of creatures in 7:8 is confirmed as saved and under covenant in 9:10.
The gathering in 7:8 is the precondition for the new dominion described in 9:2.
Noah's knowledge of clean and unclean animals in 7:8 confirms that the division mentioned in 11:47 is a resumption of an existing order.
7:2 is the command that 7:8 describes as carried out; they are directly narratively connected.
7:14 confirms that the division mentioned in 7:8 was completed at the entrance to the ark.
